hints: Start by drawing out the full structure of 2,4-dimethylhex-2-ene, paying close attention to what is attached to each end of the C=C double bond.
Look at C2 of the double bond, it is joined to two methyl groups, so ask yourself if cis-trans isomerism can happen when one end is identical.
Now check for a chiral carbon with four different groups, focus on C4 and list its four attachments to see if it can show optical isomerism.
walkthrough:
**Draw the structure clearly**

Let's build the molecule so we can see it. Hex-2-ene means a 6-carbon chain with a double bond between C2 and C3.

Add the two methyl branches at C2 and C4:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Test for cis-trans (E/Z) isomerism**

Remember, cis-trans needs two different groups on each carbon of the C=C bond.

At C2 the two groups are $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_3$. They are identical, so swapping them makes no difference. No cis-trans isomerism is possible, even though C3 has two different groups.

**Test for optical isomerism**

Remember, optical isomerism needs a chiral centre, a carbon with four different groups.

Look at C4: it is joined to $\text{H}$, to $\text{CH}_3$, to $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and to $\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. All four are different, so C4 is chiral. The molecule therefore shows optical isomerism only.

options.A: Incorrect. While C4 is chiral so optical isomerism occurs, cis-trans does not. The trap is seeing a C=C bond and assuming E/Z is automatic, but C2 has two identical methyl groups.
options.B: Incorrect. This reverses the logic. Cis-trans is impossible because one end of the double bond (C2) carries two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, and optical isomerism is present because of the chiral centre at C4.
options.C: Incorrect. It is true there is no cis-trans isomerism, but it is wrong to say there is no optical isomerism. C4 is bonded to four different groups (H, methyl, ethyl and the alkenyl group), so it is chiral.
options.D: Correct. No cis-trans isomerism because C2 of the C=C has two identical methyl substituents. Optical isomerism is shown because C4 is a chiral centre with four different groups.
